title: NameError: next_in_progress not defined in lifecycle.pick_next_bead crashes turn-end callback
description: Regression since the latest work landed. lifecycle.pick_next_bead() calls next_in_progress() (the tier-0 stranded-bead recovery branch), but lifecycle.py's 'from .beads import (...)' block (lines ~33-46) imports list_in_progress but NOT next_in_progress. At runtime this raises NameError, which propagates up through activate_next_bead -> _on_interactive_turn_end, failing the async callback every turn end. The beads.py module DOES define next_in_progress (it's a thin head-of-list wrapper over list_in_progress); it simply isn't imported into lifecycle.py.
design: Two-line fix: add 'next_in_progress,' to the import block (alphabetical position is between next_blocking_bug and next_ready). Root cause is that an import was dropped/never added when the tier-0 recovery branch was refactored to call next_in_progress instead of list_in_progress. Worth a guard test because this class of bug (function referenced but not imported) is invisible until the specific branch executes at runtime.
acceptance_criteria:
- next_in_progress is added to the 'from .beads import (...)' block in lifecycle.py
- pick_next_bead executes without NameError; the tier-0 stranded-bead recovery branch works
- _on_interactive_turn_end completes without raising
- A regression test exercises pick_next_bead's tier-0 path (or at minimum asserts every name pick_next_bead references is importable) so a missing import is caught in CI/tests, not at runtime
- bd lint / existing test suite passes
notes:
Stack trace: NameError: name 'next_in_progress' is not defined. Did you mean: list_in_progress?
  register_callbacks.py:306 _on_interactive_turn_end
  lifecycle.py:447 activate_next_bead -> if not blockers:
  lifecycle.py:393 pick_next_bead
Confirmed: lifecycle.py import block (~L33-46) has list_in_progress but not next_in_progress; beads.py:242 defines next_in_progress.

comments.author: Aaron Weegens
comments.text: Investigated: bead premise is STALE. pick_next_bead() does NOT call next_in_progress() -- since c8b3b7c (bdboard-oals) the tier-0 recovery path calls _unblocked_in_progress() -> list_in_progress(). So no NameError is possible, and adding next_in_progress to the import block would produce an F401 unused-import (anti-fix). Root cause of the false report: a STALE COMMENT at lifecycle.py:233 still claimed the path called beads.next_in_progress -- a landmine that misled the filer. Fixed that comment in 0a834ed so it matches the real code path. ruff clean; 27/27 tests pass; tier-0 recovery is already covered by test_unblocked_stranded_in_progress_is_recovered. No runtime change required.

title: Bug-discovery deadlock: 'blocked by open issues' close failure halts the whole chain
description: When the LLM judges pass a bead X that was blocked DURING its own run (an agent filed bug Y with --blocks=X per the Bug Discovery Protocol), bead-chain's auto-close calls bd close X, which bd refuses with 'blocked by open issue(s)'. The except BeadsError handler in lifecycle.close_current_bead_success treats this as a fatal infra error and calls state.stop() -- halting the ENTIRE chain. This is a deadlock, not a fault: the recovery machinery (pick_next_bead tier-0 _unblocked_strands revert + tier-1 blocking-bug routing) already exists and would self-heal, but the halt fires before it ever runs. See ADR 0004 (notes/decisions/0004-close-failure-blocked-is-recoverable.md). Fix: split the close-failure handler by error class. A 'blocked by open issues' refusal should revert the bead to open and CONTINUE; every other BeadsError keeps today's halt-loudly behavior. Add a narrow _is_blocked_close_error predicate; on a failed revert, fall back to halting.
design: Touch points: lifecycle.close_current_bead_success (the except BeadsError site, ~lifecycle.py:320-330). Add _is_blocked_close_error(exc) matching bd's 'blocked by open issue(s)' message (keep narrow; degrade to halt on no-match, which is safe). On match: emit_info, revert_to_open(bead_id), clear current_bead, do NOT state.stop(). On revert failure: warn + state.stop() (failed revert IS infra-class). Optional polish: append a judge-visible note on revert ('prior work may already satisfy criteria; verify before redoing') to cut re-drive token burn. Docs to update: close_current_bead_success docstring, WorkTimeBlockerGate.md + CloseGuard.md halt-on-close-failure narrative.
acceptance_criteria: - A 'blocked by open issues' close failure reverts the bead to open and the chain CONTINUES (does not call state.stop()).

title: Create br/ variant — adapt plugin for beads_rust compatibility
description:
Fork bd/ into br/ and apply the 5 adaptations identified in spike bead_chain-5d3:

1. DEFAULT BINARY: Change default from bd to br (beads.py binary resolution).
2. DROP --exclude-type: Remove the flag from all callers in beads_reads.py (next_ready, next_ready_in_epic, next_blocking_bug, _list_by_status). The existing client-side is_excluded_type re-filter already provides defence-in-depth — it becomes the sole filter.
3. UNWRAP LIST ENVELOPE: _parse_json_list in beads.py must handle {"issues":[...]} object shape (br list --json) in addition to the bare array (br ready --json is already an array).
4. REIMPLEMENT has_open_children: beads_reads.py — br has no list --parent=<id>. Use br list --json + client-side parent field filter instead.
5. WIDEN CLOSE_GUARD: close_guard.py _BD_INVOCATION regex must match br in addition to bd. Same for _BD_UPDATE_STATUS_CLOSED_RE. This is a SAFETY item — without it, an agent calling br close bypasses the LLM-judge close guard undetected.

Feature degradations (already soft-fail, no code changes needed):
- memories subcommand absent → prompt.py soft-fails to empty dict.
- gate subcommand absent → lifecycle.py probe_resolved_gates soft-fails.
acceptance_criteria:
- br/ directory exists with all 10 runtime .py files adapted for beads_rust.
- Default binary is br (not bd).
- --exclude-type flag removed from all _run_bd calls; client-side is_excluded_type is sole filter.
- _parse_json_list handles both bare array and {issues:[...]} object envelope.
- has_open_children works via client-side parent filter (no --parent in subprocess args).
- close_guard regex matches both br and bd binary names.
- br/ variant can be installed as bead_chain/ and starts without error when br is on PATH.

title: Sanitize bead IDs and validate BEADS_BIN before subprocess calls
description:
Two security hardening items:

1. BEAD ID SANITIZATION (beads.py _run_bd calls): Bead IDs from bd JSON output are passed directly as subprocess args. While list-form subprocess.run prevents shell injection, a maliciously crafted bead ID with special characters could cause unexpected behavior in the bd binary's argument parsing. Add a validation regex (e.g., ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$) before passing IDs to subprocess.

2. BEADS_BIN VALIDATION (beads.py:218): The BEADS_BIN env var is used unsanitized as the executable path. An attacker who can set environment variables could redirect all bd calls to an arbitrary binary. Add basic validation: resolve to absolute path, check it's a real file, optionally verify it's in a trusted directory.
acceptance_criteria:
- Bead IDs validated against a regex (e.g. ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$) before passing to subprocess.
- BEADS_BIN env var resolved to absolute path and verified as a real executable file before first use.
- Invalid bead IDs or BEADS_BIN values raise clear errors (not silent failures).
- pytest passes + new validation tests added.

title: Fix _has_fan_out_gate_issue: private API access + unbounded db query
description:
Two compounding issues in lifecycle.py:780-793:

1. PRIVATE API ACCESS: _has_fan_out_gate_issue calls beads._run_bd('list', '--json') and beads._parse_json_list() — underscore-prefixed private helpers. This creates tight coupling to beads.py implementation details and violates the module's public API contract.

2. UNBOUNDED QUERY: The function fetches the ENTIRE issue database (bd list --json with no filters) just to find children of one spawner. On a large project this is O(n) in total issues and could be extremely slow or OOM.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Have a project with thousands of beads.
2. Run /bead-chain on a bead that triggers the fan-out gate check.
3. Observe: every issue in the database is fetched and parsed just to check one spawner's children.
acceptance_criteria:
- _has_fan_out_gate_issue no longer calls beads._run_bd or beads._parse_json_list (private API).
- Uses a public helper or bd list --parent=<spawner_id> --json (scoped query, not full db scan).
- pytest passes (245 tests).
- Manually verified: fan-out gate check works correctly on a bead with waits_for children-of().

title: Research: bead-chain ↔ wiggum ↔ goal context lifecycle on bead transitions
description:
Research how context flows (or gets wiped) when bead-chain transitions between beads. The user needs to understand whether the next bead gets a clean context or inherits the accumulated conversation from the previous bead.

## Goal
Produce a documented model of the context lifecycle across the bead-chain → wiggum → goal interaction, specifically at bead close → next-bead-claim transitions. Answer: what survives, what gets wiped, and what carries over implicitly.

## What we already know (starting points in the code)
- lifecycle.py:727 returns `clear_context: True` when arming wiggum with the next bead's goal prompt. This signals code_puppy to clear conversation history.
- lifecycle.py:721 calls `wiggum_state.start(goal_prompt, mode="goal")` to hand the wheel to wiggum's /goal loop.
- register_callbacks.py documents the turn-by-turn lifecycle: wiggum judges goal-complete → stops itself → bead-chain sees wiggum inactive → closes the bead → picks next → re-arms wiggum with `clear_context: True`.
- Recovery mode (stranded in_progress bead) also goes through the same path with `recovery=True`.

## Questions to answer
1. What does `clear_context: True` actually clear in code_puppy? Full conversation history? System prompt? Tool state? Does the host respect this flag or is it advisory?
2. What SURVIVES across bead transitions despite clear_context? (bd memories, AGENTS.md/system prompt, bd prime context, execution hints, plugin state, wiggum config?)
3. What does `format_bead_as_goal()` inject as the new context? How much of the previous bead's work is summarized or referenced?
4. In recovery mode, does the recovered bead get any context about what was done before the crash, or just a fresh goal prompt + recovery preamble?
5. Is there any mechanism for carrying insights/notes from bead N to bead N+1 (e.g., via bd update --append-notes on the next bead, or bd remember)?
6. How does wiggum's /goal mode interact — does wiggum maintain its own state across bead-chain iterations, or does it fully reset on each `wiggum_state.start()` call?
7. Are there scenarios where context SHOULD carry over but doesn't (e.g., related beads that share domain knowledge), or where it carries over but shouldn't?
design: Read lifecycle.py (activate_next_bead, the return dict), prompt.py (format_bead_as_goal), register_callbacks.py (turn lifecycle docs), and the wiggum plugin state module. May need to read code_puppy host code to understand what clear_context actually does. Experimental validation: run /bead-chain on 2 sequential beads and observe whether conversation messages from bead 1 appear in bead 2's context.
acceptance_criteria:
- Documented model of the context lifecycle across bead transitions (what clears, what persists, what's injected).
- Each of the 7 questions answered with evidence (code refs or experimental observation).
- Diagram or table showing the context layers (conversation history, system prompt, bd memories, plugin state, wiggum state) and their behavior at bead close → next claim.
- Identified any gaps or risks (e.g., context that should carry over but doesn't, or vice versa).
- Findings recorded in bead notes.
- Timeboxed to 90 min.

title: Fix formula tracking and align FlowDoc formulas with bd schema
description:
The FlowDoc formulas (flowdoc-generate, flowdoc-html, flowdoc-maintain) and code-health-audit formula have structural issues that prevent proper pour tracking. The root cause is that the `parent` field in formula steps creates molecule-internal hierarchy but NOT bd-level parent-child edges, so bd epic close-eligible, bd list --parent, and bd dep tree never see the children. Result: root epics get stuck open and molecules can never complete.

Additionally, the formulas use several fields not in the verified bd formula step schema (training volume V, § I.5): parent, waits_for, labels, skills, priority. Some of these work (waits_for, labels) and some don't wire as expected (parent). None of the formulas set phase: liquid (recommended for poured formulas per § IV).

NOTE: formula work is NOT part of the bead-chain plugin itself. Formulas are authored under .beads/formulas/ and are used BY bead-chain but are separate concerns. Keep this distinction clear.

## Success Criteria
- The tracking issue is understood and resolved: when a formula is poured, its steps are visible as bd-level children of the root epic (or the correct workaround is documented).
- All FlowDoc formulas pass bd cook --dry-run without warnings and align with the verified formula schema.
- Existing stuck molecules are cleaned up.
- A bd remember captures the formula authoring patterns for future formula work.

title: Investigate: does formula `parent` field create bd-level parent-child edges on pour?
description:
Timeboxed investigation (90 min). The parent field in formula steps creates molecule-internal hierarchy (visible in bd mol show/current) but NOT bd-level parent-child dependency edges. This means bd epic close-eligible, bd list --parent, and bd dep tree don't see the children, so root epics get stuck open forever.

NOTE: This is formula infrastructure work, not bead-chain plugin code.

## Goal
Determine whether the formula step parent field is a supported bd schema field that should create bd-level parent-child edges on pour (potential bd bug), or whether it is mol-internal only (by design) and a different pattern is needed. Also verify which other extra step fields (waits_for, labels, skills, priority) are supported vs silently ignored. Output: documented findings + the correct formula authoring pattern, recorded in bead notes.

## Questions
1. Is parent a supported formula step field in bd 1.0.5? (Training volume V § I.5 does NOT list it.)
2. If supported, does it create bd-level parent-child edges on pour, or only mol-internal hierarchy?
3. If NOT supported / mol-internal only, what is the correct formula pattern for bd-level parent-child wiring?
4. What about waits_for, labels, skills, priority — which are recognized vs silently ignored?

## Approach
Create a minimal test formula with parent + depends_on, pour it, check bd list --parent, bd dep tree, bd epic close-eligible. Compare behavior with and without parent. Check bd mol pour --help and bd cook --help for field documentation. Reference training volume V (field-guide-05-formulas-and-molecules/OUTLINE.md). Clean up test artifacts (bd mol burn) after.
acceptance_criteria:
- Q1 answered: documented whether parent is a supported formula step field in bd 1.0.5.
- Q2 answered: determined whether parent creates bd-level parent-child edges on pour or only mol-internal hierarchy, with evidence (test formula poured + checked via bd list --parent + bd dep tree).
- Q3 answered: if parent doesn't wire bd-level edges, the correct formula pattern for bd-level parent-child wiring is identified and documented.
- Q4 answered: waits_for, labels, skills, priority verified as recognized/ignored.
- Findings recorded in bead notes (not just closed — the spike output IS the notes).
- Timeboxed to 90 min.
notes:
## Spike Findings (recorded in notes/spikes/formula-parent-field-investigation-eq8.md)

### TL;DR
- parent field: SILENTLY IGNORED by pour. All steps become flat children of the mol root. Formulas cannot create bd-level parent-child hierarchies. This breaks bd list --parent, bd dep tree, and bd epic close-eligible for formula-defined epics.
- skills field: SILENTLY IGNORED by pour. Not present in created beads.
- labels: WORKS. Correctly applied to created beads.
- priority: WORKS. Correctly applied.
- depends_on: WORKS. Creates proper blocks edges between steps.
- waits_for: UNTESTED (uses formula-level children-of(X) syntax, needs separate investigation).

### Root cause
Pour translates some step fields (type, title, description, priority, labels, depends_on) to bd create flags but does NOT translate parent or skills. The parent field is accepted without error (no schema validation), silently dropped, and all steps are parented to the molecule root instead.

### Correct pattern (today)
Post-pour fixup: bd update <child> --parent <epic> after pour. Tedious but works.

### Recommended fix
File a bd bug: parent should either be wired to --parent on created beads or rejected with an explicit error. Silent drop is the worst outcome. Same for skills.

title: Add gated soft-fail bd dolt push to AGENTS.md session-close (impl of FB-4/ADR-0001)
description:
Implements the decision recorded in docs/decisions/0001-dolt-push-lives-in-session-close.md (bead_chain-uo4 / FB-4): sync responsibility lives in the session-close protocol, NOT in bead-chain's drain path.

Scope:
- Add an explicit `bd dolt push` step to the AGENTS.md 'Session Completion' mandatory workflow, immediately AFTER `git push`.
- Gate it on a configured Dolt remote (`bd dolt remote list` non-empty) and soft-fail (warn, do not halt) when no remote is configured or the push errors.
- Document that interrupted chains (Ctrl+C/cancel) are local-only until the next session-close runs `bd dolt push`.
- Document that CI / disposable-agent environments are responsible for invoking `bd dolt push` in their own teardown (they are just another caller of session-close).
- Do NOT modify lifecycle.py / the drain path. bead-chain stays sync-agnostic by design (queue-driver-not-goal-engine SRP boundary).

## Acceptance Criteria
- AGENTS.md session-close workflow contains a `bd dolt push` step after `git push`, described as gated-on-remote and soft-fail.
- The interrupted-chain local-only caveat and the CI/disposable teardown responsibility are documented (AGENTS.md and/or the ADR cross-reference).
- No change to lifecycle.py drain path (no dolt push/pull/export/import added to the queue driver).
- Cross-references docs/decisions/0001-dolt-push-lives-in-session-close.md.

title: FB-1: Exclude milestone/gate/molecule from EXCLUDED_TYPES (chain stalls on leaked container beads)
description:
EXCLUDED_TYPES = ("epic",) (beads.py:41) only excludes epics. milestone (anatomy#4), gate (gates#2) and molecule (swarms#1) are container/handle types that can appear as ready leaves on `bd ready`; next_ready() hands them to /goal as if they were code work. They have nothing to do, and close_guard then blocks closing them -> the chain stalls. This is the highest-leverage fix: one constant edit closes three P1 stall hazards. The existing server-side --exclude-type + client-side is_excluded_type double filter already supports a tuple.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Have a ready milestone/gate/molecule bead on the `bd ready` frontier.
2. Run /bead-chain.
3. The container bead is claimed and driven through /goal; it has no code work; close_guard blocks closing it -> loop stalls.

## Acceptance Criteria
- EXCLUDED_TYPES covers epic, milestone, gate, molecule.
- A ready milestone/gate/molecule is never returned by next_ready()/pick_next_bead (server- and client-side).
- Regression test mirrors the existing epic-exclusion tests for each new type.

title: FB-4: Decide where `bd dolt push` lives in the bead-chain end-to-end loop
description:
Nobody in the documented loop runs `bd dolt push`: bead-chain drain (lifecycle.py:517-524) does not, and AGENTS.md session-close pushes refs/heads/* not refs/dolt/data. On a single box this is harmless; on fresh clone / CI / second machine every claim/close/revert is stranded locally (the embedded Dolt DB is git-ignored). Needs a human policy call, not just code.

## Rationale
Cross-machine durability currently falls through a seam between bead-chain and the AGENTS.md session-close protocol. We must decide who owns refs/dolt/data sync so claims/closes are not stranded locally.

## Alternatives Considered
- (a) bead-chain pushes on successful drain when `bd dolt remote` is non-empty (soft-fail).
- (b) Add `bd dolt push` to the AGENTS.md session-close protocol.
- (c) Explicitly document local-only as intended (no code change).

## Success Criteria
- A written decision recorded (in this beads notes / an ADR) on where sync responsibility lives.
- If (a) or (b): a concrete follow-up implementation task is filed.
notes: DECISION (FB-4): Option (b) — bd dolt push lives in the AGENTS.md session-close protocol, gated on a configured Dolt remote and soft-failing; bead-chain stays sync-agnostic (no change to the drain path). Rationale: bead-chain is a queue driver not a sync engine (queue-driver-not-goal-engine SRP boundary); durability already lives next to git push in session-close; a drain is not a session boundary; CI/disposable agents are just another caller of session-close. Rejected (a) push-on-drain (wrong cadence + SRP violation; kept only as a possible future safety net) and (c) local-only (leaves a known P1 footgun). Full record: docs/decisions/0001-dolt-push-lives-in-session-close.md. Follow-up implementation task filed under epic bead_chain-2p3.

- Failure warns and never halts the loop.

title: Diátaxis: generate maintainer documentation
description:
Umbrella for a from-scratch Diátaxis documentation pass (maintainer edition).

Diátaxis organises docs around FOUR USER NEEDS, located on a 2×2 compass
(research/tech/diataxis-documentation-framework-research.md; ADR flowdoc-yuw):
  Navigate by two questions — action or cognition? acquisition or application?
    - action  + acquisition  -> tutorial      (learning-oriented)
    - action  + application  -> how-to guide   (goal/task-oriented)
    - cognition + application -> reference      (information-oriented)
    - cognition + acquisition -> explanation    (understanding-oriented)
This REPLACES the legacy features/flows/endpoints/views/concepts taxonomy,
which was product-led — the exact failure mode Diátaxis cures.

AUDIENCE MAP (read this first, every child obeys it):
  - audience = maintainer -> write to diataxis/maintainer/ ; voice = for
    developers/contributors; may include implementation detail, source file
    paths, code blocks, mermaid, API/View tables, internal/build commands.
  - audience = user       -> write to diataxis/user/       ; voice = for end
    users; NO source paths, NO code, NO internal/localhost/staging URLs, NO dev-setup/build/test instructions; task/outcome oriented.
The audience overlay constrains a doc's allowed surface detail only — it never
overrides a type's Diátaxis orientation.

This epic has exactly two authored children: 'discover' (runs first and spawns
one bead per documentation item, each classified by the compass) and 'finalize'
(runs last, gated on every doc). Do not work this epic directly — work
its leaves.

title: Spike: handle recursive formula pours / nested epics under the single-in_progress invariant
description: A formula pour can spawn beads that are themselves epics, and those epics can pour again (recursive formula pours). This means an arbitrarily deep epic hierarchy can have N epics legitimately in_progress at once — one per level of the active branch — while the chain still maintains its core contract of exactly ONE non-epic (doable) bead in_progress at a time. Today the code tolerates multiple in_progress epics only incidentally (list_in_progress passes --exclude-type=epic), and ensure_epic_in_progress only claims the bead's DIRECT parent — it does not walk the ancestor chain. We need to investigate whether deep nesting breaks epic activation, rollup/close-eligibility, recovery, and status displays, then produce a plan.
design: Grounding in current code (bead_chain plugin): lifecycle.enforce_single_in_progress (head-recovery, leaves extras in_progress), lifecycle.ensure_epic_in_progress (claims ONLY extract_parent_epic_id(bead) — the direct parent), lifecycle.rollup_completed_epics + beads.close_eligible_epics (epic auto-close), beads.list_in_progress/next_in_progress (filter epics via --exclude-type=epic so multiple in_progress epics are already silently allowed). Timebox the investigation; the deliverable is a decision + follow-up beads, not a fix.

2. Create and complete all child beads under that epic
3. Observe the epic does not roll up / show as complete-eligible, unlike a standard epic (bdboard-isk) in the same situation

Suspected root cause: three-segment formula id format (bdboard-mol-isk) not matched by rollup logic that expects two-segment epic ids (bdboard-isk).
design: Investigate the rollup logic's assumptions about epic id structure. Compare how standard epic ids (bdboard-isk) vs formula epic ids (bdboard-mol-isk) are parsed/matched during rollup. If id parsing assumes two segments, extend to tolerate the extra formula segment.

- Root cause of the missing rollup identified and documented in notes/design
- Confirmed whether the bdboard-mol-isk id format is the cause
- Rollup works for formula-derived epics: completing all children marks/treats the epic as eligible for rollup the same as standard epics
- Regression coverage added for formula-derived epic ids
notes:
ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION (code-puppy-55a19c):

The bead-chain plugin performs ZERO id-segment parsing anywhere. Rollup is fully delegated to 'bd epic close-eligible' (see beads.close_eligible_epics / lifecycle.rollup_completed_epics). grep for split/rsplit/partition/regex on ids returns nothing. So the suspected 'two-segment epic id parser that breaks on bdboard-mol-isk' does not exist in this codebase.

Empirical repro on bd 1.0.4 (embedded Dolt): created a standard 2-segment epic (test-aaa) and a 3-segment formula-style epic (test-mol-bbb), each with one child. Closed both children, then ran 'bd epic status --eligible-only --json' and 'bd epic close-eligible --json'. BOTH epics reported eligible_for_close:true and BOTH were rolled up/closed. Repeated with epics marked in_progress FIRST (the exact bead-chain sequence: claim epic -> close child -> rollup) — again BOTH 2-seg and 3-seg ids rolled up correctly.

title: test_version hardcodes stale 0.1.0 assertion (actual 0.2.1)
description:
[bead-chain:triaged] test_version_is_defined_and_is_0_1_0 asserted init.__version__ == '0.1.0' but bd/__init__.py has been 0.2.1 since the v0.2.0 marketplace remediation release. Pre-existing on HEAD (verified via git show HEAD:__init__.py + git show HEAD:tests/test_version.py) — NOT caused by the bd/ subdir move (bead_chain-4v9). It blocked bead_chain-4v9's "all tests pass" acceptance criterion. Originally fixed inline by updating the assertion+docstring to 0.2.1 to match the single-source version; this bead then upgraded that band-aid to a source-shape assertion so version bumps don't re-break it (commit 18d2e13).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On HEAD, bd/__init__.py defines the single source of truth __version__ = "0.2.1" (since the v0.2.0 marketplace remediation release).
2. tests/test_version.py asserted `init.__version__ == "0.1.0"` in test_version_is_defined_and_is_0_1_0.
3. Run `python3 -m pytest tests/test_version.py` — the equality assertion fails (0.2.1 != 0.1.0), turning the suite red and blocking the "all tests pass" criterion of bead_chain-4v9.

## Root Cause
The test hardcoded the version literal, so it silently drifted from the single source of truth (bd/__init__.py) on every version bump.

## Fix
Replaced the hardcoded literal equality with a strict MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH shape check (_VERSION_RE, PEP 440-ish suffix allowed) and renamed the test to test_version_is_defined_and_well_formed. Runtime<->source literal consistency stays enforced by the existing test_version_is_greppable_from_source (which greps bd/__init__.py and compares to the runtime value) — mirroring the source-derived pattern in tests/test_release_checksum.py. No coverage lost; the test can no longer re-break on a routine version bump.
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_version.py passes; the version assertion no longer hardcodes a literal (a routine version bump must not re-red the suite); runtime<->source literal consistency stays locked by test_version_is_greppable_from_source; ruff check/format clean; full suite green.

Proper fix landed in commit 18d2e13: replaced literal equality with a strict MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH shape check (_VERSION_RE), renamed to test_version_is_defined_and_well_formed. No coverage lost (greppable source<->runtime cross-check retained). Full suite: 367 passed. Bead left OPEN for judges to close.

title: Investigate beads_rust (br) as drop-in replacement for bd in bead-chain
description:
Investigate whether a bead-chain user can set BEADS_BIN=br and use https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust instead of bd (Python beads CLI). bead-chain already supports swapping the binary via BEADS_BIN with validation — the question is whether br's CLI surface, JSON output schema, and behavioral contracts are compatible.

## Goal
Determine whether br is a drop-in replacement for bd from bead-chain's perspective, identify any compatibility gaps, and recommend whether to officially support it (and what that would take).

## What bead-chain depends on from the bd CLI
bead-chain invokes bd as a subprocess via beads.py. The full surface area to check:

**Commands used** (grep _run_bd across the codebase):
- bd list --json (with --status, --parent filters)
- bd show <id> --json
- bd ready --json
- bd search <query> --json
- bd update <id> --claim / --append-notes / --description / --design / --notes / --status
- bd close <id> --reason <text>
- bd lint --json
- bd memories <topic>
- bd dep tree <id>
- bd dep cycles
- bd blocked <id>
- bd epic close-eligible

**JSON output schema dependencies** (beads._parse_json_list, field access throughout):
- Issue fields: id, title, type, status, priority, description, acceptance, design, notes, labels, assignee, parent, metadata, estimate, created_at, updated_at
- Dep/edge fields: from, to, type
- Status values: open, in_progress, closed, blocked, deferred
- Priority values: P0-P4 (or 0-4 integer)

**Behavioral contracts**:
- --claim is atomic (returns error if already claimed by another)
- --json flag produces parseable JSON (array for list/ready/search, object for show)
- Exit code 0 = success, non-zero = error
- Error messages parseable for specific conditions (BeadsError handling)

## Approach
1. Read the beads_rust README and docs — what commands does br support? What's the CLI surface?
2. Compare br's command names, flags, and JSON output format against the list above.
3. If br is available to install, run a smoke test: BEADS_BIN=br bd list --json and compare output with bd list --json on the same repo.
4. Check: does br use the same .beads/ directory structure? Same Dolt backend? Or a different storage model?
5. Check: does br support bd dolt push/pull, or does it have its own sync mechanism?
6. Identify gaps: commands missing, flags missing, JSON schema differences, behavioral differences.
7. Assess: is br a strict superset, a compatible subset, or a divergent fork?

## Output
- Compatibility matrix (command × supported/missing/different)
- List of breaking differences that would require bead-chain code changes
- Recommendation: drop-in / needs adapter / incompatible
- If adapter needed: estimate of work to support both backends
acceptance_criteria:
- beads_rust repo README and CLI docs reviewed.
- Compatibility matrix produced: every bd command/flag bead-chain uses mapped to br equivalent (or 'missing').
- JSON output schema compared for at least: list, show, ready, search.
- Storage model compatibility assessed (.beads/ dir, Dolt, sync).
- Breaking differences enumerated with specific code locations in bead-chain that would need changes.
- Recommendation documented: drop-in / adapter / incompatible.
- Findings recorded in bead notes.
- Timeboxed to 120 min.
notes: SPIKE COMPLETE (see notes/spikes/beads-rust-br-drop-in-compat-5d3.md, commit 061af41). Verdict: br (beads_rust v0.2.15) is NOT a drop-in for bd. Method: audited every _run_bd() call site for the real surface, installed br 0.2.15, ran each exact invocation. Compatible: update --claim, update --status=open, close --reason, show --json, lint --status all --json, epic close-eligible. BREAKING (any one chain-fatal): (A) no --exclude-type on ready/list (exit 2); (B) br list --json returns object {issues:[...]} not array -> breaks _parse_json_list + has_epic_in_progress; (C) no list --parent -> breaks has_open_children. Soft-fail feature loss: no memories subcommand, no gate subcommand. Bonus: close_guard._BD_INVOCATION matches only basename 'bd' -> agent 'br close' bypasses judge guard. Storage: SQLite+JSONL, no Dolt (plugin code unaffected; AGENTS.md dolt-push workflow N/A). Failure mode graceful: first selection read raises BeadsError -> activate_next_bead -> state.stop(). Recommendation: (1) document br as unsupported + (3) reject br loudly at startup (~1-2h); build adapter (~1-1.5d) only if demand appears. All acceptance criteria met. NOT closing - judges to verify.

description: _BD_CLOSE_RE and _BD_UPDATE_STATUS_CLOSED_RE in close_guard.py are compiled with re.MULTILINE, so _COMMAND_BOUNDARY (^|&&|||;|) also matches the start of every EMBEDDED line, not just the start of the whole command. - Unknown keys are ignored; absent metadata -> no change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A stranded in_progress bead gated by a generic waits-for is reverted, not re-driven.
- Regression test covers the recovery-tier path.

The 6 context-bearing edges (related, relates-to, tracks, discovered-from, caused-by, validates) are never surfaced (dependency#2); the agent works blind to provenance, causal bug links and validating tests. Correct to ignore for gating; this is about context. Can ride with FB-2/FB-7 prompt work.

## Acceptance Criteria
- When present, discovered-from/caused-by/validates/related appear as a 'related context' block in the goal prompt.
- Gating behavior is unchanged.

Prepend a `bd memories` (or `bd prime` '## Persistent Memories') digest into format_bead_as_goal, and add a 'record durable insights via bd remember --key=' step to the done-checklist. Decide the bd-memories <-> host Kennel policy (bridge vs document the split).

- The goal prompt includes a memory digest when memories exist.
- The done-checklist nudges `bd remember`.
- A one-line policy note on the bd/Kennel split is recorded.

Workaround applied in this bead: post-processed the 3 generated HTML files under docs/ to fix the anchors; source markdown under diataxis/ is read-only and was not touched. Suggested fix: normalize whitespace/newlines inside link text before regex, and add a post-build guard that greps output HTML for unconverted `\[.*\]\(.*\.md\)` and fails the build.

- **SOLID:** Check single responsibility (are modules focused?), open/closed (can behavior be extended without modification?), dependency inversion (are high-level modules decoupled from low-level details?).

title: Optimize retry backoff — 91.5s worst case is too aggressive

Consider: shorter initial timeout, exponential backoff with lower ceiling, or fail-fast on known-fatal errors.

title: Decide: move ADR-style inline comments to notes/decisions/ or keep inline
description:
The review flags excessive inline documentation — many functions have docstrings and comments longer than the code (e.g., open_blocker_ids: ~40 lines of docstring for ~15 lines of logic). Design rationale currently lives inline as ADR-style comments.

## Rationale
The inline comments serve as living documentation that stays co-located with the code they explain. Moving them to separate ADR files risks them going stale. But the volume makes navigation harder.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Keep inline, trim to essential context only (remove historical rationale, keep the 'why').
2. Move all ADR-style content to notes/decisions/ files, leave concise docstrings inline.
3. Hybrid: keep concise docstrings inline, move lengthy design rationale to a single DESIGN.md with code cross-references.
4. No change — the verbosity is acceptable given the plugin's complexity.

- Decision captured in notes/decisions/ as an ADR with Rationale and Alternatives Considered.

title: Move bd subprocess calls off the event loop (async hooks block UI)
description:
The async callback hooks in register_callbacks.py call synchronous subprocess.run(bd ...) directly rather than via asyncio.to_thread() or a thread executor. A slow bd call blocks the UI event loop during bead activation.

Well-mitigated today: 15s timeout, ~45s worst case with retries, and an immediate 'starting…' ack before the blocking call. This is the established design and non-blocking for release. But it violates the async iron-rule (never block the event loop) and could become painful if bd latency increases or the project grows.

The fix is wrapping _run_bd calls in asyncio.to_thread() (or equivalent) so the event loop stays responsive during subprocess execution. Needs care: the current sequential call pattern has implicit ordering guarantees that must be preserved.
acceptance_criteria:
- All bd subprocess calls from async hooks run in a thread executor (asyncio.to_thread or loop.run_in_executor).
- UI remains responsive during bead activation (no event-loop blocking).
- Sequential ordering of bd calls within a single activation is preserved (no race conditions from premature parallelism).
- 15s timeout and retry behavior unchanged.
- pytest passes.

The plugin loader catches this and the app survives, but the user sees a cryptic traceback rather than a friendly 'bead-chain requires the wiggum plugin' message.

This is by-design (README documents wiggum as a prerequisite) and non-blocking. The improvement is purely UX: catch the ImportError at the top of register_callbacks.py, log a clear message, and either gracefully degrade or raise a cleaner error.

title: FlowDoc HTML build clobbers hand-authored user-facing docs/ guides (directory collision)
description:
Found while validating the rebuilt maintainer HTML site (bead_chain-mol-dro). UNRELATED to the validation rubric, so filed separately per Bug Discovery Protocol. NON-BLOCKING: the built site could still be scored.

WHAT I SAW: `git status` after the FlowDoc-html build shows the hand-authored user-facing guides DELETED from the working tree:
  D docs/README.md
  D docs/getting-started.md
  D docs/usage.md
  D docs/troubleshooting.md
All four still exist in git HEAD (git show HEAD:docs/README.md succeeds), so this is an uncommitted working-tree regression introduced by the build step (bead_chain-mol-d79 / flowdoc-html mol-33a). docs/index.html was also overwritten — it is now the FlowDoc edition landing page (<title>bead-chain Documentation</title>, links docs/maintainer/) rather than the user-facing README index.

ROOT CAUSE (collision): per the docs-vs-notes convention (bead_chain-bch), docs/ is the home of USER-FACING task-oriented guides (README + getting-started/usage/troubleshooting). But the FlowDoc-html target ALSO publishes into docs/ (docs/maintainer/, docs/user/, docs/index.html). The build evidently cleans/regenerates docs/ destructively, wiping the hand-authored .md guides. Two doc systems claim the same directory.

IMPACT: the real user-facing documentation is silently destroyed every time the FlowDoc HTML site is (re)built. Since these are uncommitted deletions, a `git checkout -- docs/*.md` recovers them now — but the next build will nuke them again.

SUGGESTED FIX (pick one, design decision for maintainer):
  1. Publish the FlowDoc HTML site to a dedicated subdir (e.g. docs/flowdoc/ or a separate site/ root) instead of docs/ root, leaving docs/*.md untouched; OR
  2. Make the FlowDoc-html build clean ONLY its own output namespace (docs/maintainer/, docs/user/, and a clearly-owned docs/index.html) and never touch sibling .md files; OR
  3. Move user-facing guides out of docs/ and formally cede docs/ to the generated site.
Whichever is chosen, the build must be non-destructive toward files it does not own.

REPRO: run the flowdoc-html build into docs/, then `git status` — observe the four docs/*.md deletions. RECOVERY: `git checkout -- docs/README.md docs/getting-started.md docs/usage.md docs/troubleshooting.md`.
close_reason: FALSE POSITIVE / not-a-bug — won't fix. The docs/*.md deletions the build agent observed were INTENTIONAL maintainer edits, not a build-step regression. Decision: FlowDoc-authored docs supersede hand-authored ones, so docs/ is deliberately ceded to the generated FlowDoc HTML site (this is option 3 from the bug's own suggested-fix list). The hand-authored README/getting-started/usage/troubleshooting were removed on purpose; any surviving hand-authored artifacts now live in notes/ (per the docs-vs-notes convention, bead_chain-feu/bch). There is therefore no collision and nothing to recover — do NOT git checkout the deleted files. The FlowDoc-html build (mol-d79/mol-33a) owning docs/ is correct, intended behavior.
